_comment: Built-in dialogue, used when the AI is unavailable (and for ordinary townsfolk). {slots}: name (theirs), player (the player's first name), place (the settlement), job (their occupation), title (theirs), size (a word for the place), plus others where noted. greeting: by how they feel about you. special: built-in skill-check options (the AI proposes its own when it can); outcome ids are the same whitelist the AI chooses from.

hostile: They look at you the way you'd look at a rat in the flour.
"Walk on. Whatever it is, walk on."
"You have a nerve, coming to my door."
They spit, not quite at your feet, and wait.
unfriendly: They don't stop what they're doing.
"If it's work you want, it isn't here."
They look you over once and are not impressed.
"We get a lot of your sort through {place}."
neutral: "Good day to you. Or what passes for one."
They straighten up and wait to hear what you want.
They nod, the way you nod at weather.
friendly: "Ah, it's you. Come in, come in."
"Good to see a face that isn't trouble."
"You look like you've walked a way. Sit down before you fall down."
"Now there's a welcome sight. What news?"
"Come in out of it, whatever it is doing out there."
warm: "Friend. What can I do for you?"
"{player}. I was only saying your name the other day."
"Whatever you want, it's yours, and we'll argue about the price after."
They take your hand in both of theirs.

innkeeper: "There's a fire and there's stew. Both cost."
serving_hand: "With you in a moment — mind your feet."
priest: "You've come a long way for a small church."
"Kneel if you like. Talk if you'd rather."
acolyte: "Oh — hello. Were you looking for the priest?"
"I'm only sweeping. But I can listen."
smith: "Speak up, I'm half deaf from the hammer."
"If it's broken, put it on the bench."
shopkeeper: "Whatever it is, I've likely got it. Somewhere."
healer: "Are you hurt, or is it someone else?"
"Sit down and let me see it."
"Wash your hands before you touch anything in here."
stablemaster: "You'll be wanting a horse, or wanting rid of one."
headman: "You'll be the traveller they told me about."
"{place} is a quiet place. We like it quiet."
lord: "Be brief. I have the assizes at noon."
They let the silence go on a moment longer than is comfortable.
market_trader: "Best price in {place}, and I'll not go lower."
guard: Their hand stays where it was, near the hilt.
farmer: "Aye?" They don't put the fork down.
"If you've come about the field, I've said my piece."
labourer: They wipe their hands and wait.
carter: "I'm going out at first light if you want the road."
beggar: "Bless you — before you've even given me anything."
fisher: "Tide's wrong for talking, but go on."
"Smell of it doesn't bother you? Good."
woodcutter: "Aye. Say it quick, the light's going."
adventurer: "Another one. Come to make your name?"
"You have the look. Sword or spells?"
miner: "You've come up from the road, then. I've come up from worse."

remember_threat: "You're the one who threatened me. I haven't forgotten."
"You. You've a nerve, coming back after what you said to me."
"I remember your face. And what came out of it."
They take a step back before you have said a word. "I remember you."
"Say what you want and go. I've not forgotten last time."
"Back again. I remember what you said to me, if you don't."
remember_help: "I owe you one. I haven't forgotten that either."
"It's you! Sit down, sit down. I haven't forgotten what you did."
"Well met. I still owe you for last time."
"You're welcome here, after what you did. Always."
"My friend. What can I do for you?"
who_are_you: "{name}. Been the {job} here longer than I care to count."
"The name's {name}, I'm the {job}, and that's all you need to know."
"{name}. {job}. You're not from round here, are you?"
"{name}. And you'll be the stranger everyone's been talking about."
who_are_you_ruler: "I am {full}. You are in my hall."
"{full}. Most who come before me know that already."
"You are speaking to {full}. Choose your next words with care."
"I am {full}, and this land is mine. While you stand in it, so are you."
A servant answers for them: "This is {full}." The eyes that go with the name do not leave you.
"{full}. You may have heard the name. You will hear it again."
tell_about_self: "Me? Nothing anyone would put in a song."
"It's an old story, and not a happy one."
"What do you want to know that for? Well. All right."
"You'll hear worse from the rest of the town. Here's the truth of it."
They are quiet a moment, then shrug.

size_line.hamlet: A few houses and a lot of mud.
size_line.village: A village like any other: fields, a well, a temple, and everybody knows your business.
size_line.town: A market town. Busy on market days, dull the rest.
size_line.city: A city. Keep a hand on your purse.
size_line.hold: The hold. Stone above and stone below, and good steel from the forges.
size_line.elfhall: The hall among the trees. We keep to ourselves.

no_rumours: "I keep my head down. You should too."
"Nothing since I last saw you, and that was this morning."
"Ask me tomorrow. Something always happens by tomorrow."
"If I hear anything I'll not be telling it twice in one day."
rumour_intro: "You didn't hear it from me, but..."
"Since you're asking, and since nobody else will tell you..."
"There's talk. There's always talk. This week it's this."
"You want news? News costs nothing here, which tells you what it's worth."
"A carter came through and left this behind him:"
flavour_rumours: "The lord's steward is skimming the tithe. Everyone knows. Nobody says."
"Two carts went missing on the east road last month. Just the carts. No sign of the carters."
"Grain's going to be dear this winter. Mark my words."
"There's a man in the tavern paying good silver for wolf pelts."
"The miller's wife ran off with a tinker. Took the mule, too."
"Somebody's been digging in the old graveyard at night."
"The priest says the fever last spring was a judgement. On what, he didn't say."
"Soldiers came through asking about deserters. Hanged two by the crossroads."
"A woman in the next valley had a child with grey eyes. Both of them, grey right through."
"The miller's dog won't go near the old mill any more. Neither will the miller."
"Somebody's been leaving bread and milk at the boundary stone. Somebody's been taking it."
"Three men went up the hill to dig where the grass grows wrong. Two came down."
"The tithe barn was full in autumn and it isn't now, and the steward has a new horse."
"They pulled a fish out of the river with a ring in its belly. Gold. Nobody claimed it."
"The church bell rang at midnight and the rope was still tied off."
"A pedlar says the passes are worse this year than anyone alive remembers."
"There's a house in the north end that's been sold three times this year."
danger_rumour: "Keep off the {direction} road if you can. {threat}."
"Folk coming in from the {direction} have a look about them. {threat}."

threat_words.dead: Things that should be in their graves
threat_words.cult: Folk in robes, doing things in the woods at night
threat_words.monsters: Something big, that nobody has seen twice

person_lines: I'd count my fingers after shaking hands.
Good at their trade, I'll give them that.
Drinks more than is good for anyone.
Honest, which is rarer than it should be.
Wouldn't trust them to hold my coat.
Kind to children and dogs. Make of that what you like.
Knows more than they let on.
Hasn't been the same since the winter.
threaten_success: They go pale. "All right, all right. Just... calm down."
"No need for that. No need at all." Their hands are shaking.
"All right! All right. What do you want?"
They swallow, and look past you for help that is not coming.
"There's no call for that." Their voice has gone thin.
They put both hands where you can see them.
threaten_failure: "Is that a threat? In {place}? Try it."
They laugh at you. It is not a nice laugh.
"Go on, then. See how far it gets you."
"I've been threatened by better than you, and I'm still here."
They look you up and down, and go back to what they were doing.
"Say that again, louder, so the whole street can hear."
bribe_accept: The coin disappears. "Well. Maybe I can help after all."
"Generous. Very generous." Suddenly they're your friend.
They weigh the coin in a palm, and it is gone. "What was it you wanted?"
"I never saw this." The coin goes under the counter.
A quick look over the shoulder, and the money is not there any more.
bribe_refuse: "Keep your money. I'm not for sale."
They look at the coin, then at you, with contempt.
"You think that buys me? Get out."
"Not for that. Not for any money."
They push the coin back to you without a word.
refuse_talk: "I said I've nothing to say to you."
They turn their back on you.
closed: "We're shut. Come back in the morning."
A voice through the door: "Closed! Morning!"
goodbye: "If you come back, come back with news."
They are already looking past you.

success.line: "...It's nothing. All right: it's not nothing." They tell you what's been keeping them up at night.

failure.line: "I don't know what you mean. Are we done?"

any.text: [Persuasion] Tell them about your travels and win them over.

success.line: They laugh despite themselves. "You've been about, I'll give you that."

failure.line: They listen politely and are not impressed.

merchant.text: [Persuasion] Ask for a better price, as a friend.

success.line: "Ach. Fine. For you, a little off."

failure.line: "Friends pay full price. That's what makes them friends."

innkeeper.text: [Insight] Ask what they overhear from the drinkers.

success.line: "Drinkers talk. Innkeepers listen." They lean closer.

failure.line: "I hear a lot of nonsense. Most of it I forget."

guard.text: [Intimidation] Ask whether the watch is actually good for anything.

success.line: Stung, the guard tells you exactly what the watch knows and isn't doing about it.

failure.line: "Move along, before I find a reason to lock you up."
